what: Demonstration laser products must meet Class I, IIa, II or IIIa limits; projectors are limited to 5 mW visible unless the FDA approves a variance under 21 CFR 1010.4.
audience_scanning: Not addressed in the regulation text; handled through variance conditions

what: Variance conditions, binding on the variance holder rather than a regulation of general application: laser light above Class I limits kept 3.0 m above and 2.5 m lateral to or below where the public may be; operator in direct control; FAA notice for open airspace.
audience_scanning: Not permitted except diffuse reflections from the atmosphere, added scattering media and target screens; specific approval needed

what: Eligible Class IIIb/IV show variances roll over one year at a time if the annual report (due September 1) is filed.
audience_scanning: Audience scanning variances excluded from the streamlined renewal

what: Notice of outdoor laser operations requested at least 30 days before the event; flight zone limits of 50 nW/cm2 (Laser Free), 5 microwatts/cm2 (Critical), 100 microwatts/cm2 (Sensitive) and the MPE elsewhere; FAA issues a letter of determination.
Knowingly aiming a laser pointer beam at an aircraft or its flight path is punishable by fine, up to 5 years, or both.
Registration of laser installations and mobile lasers; certificate of competence to operate a mobile laser; owners name a laser safety officer. No light-show-specific section.
Class 3B and 4 lasers registered; a registration certificate and valid FDA variance before any light show; written notice 7 days before each show.
Written notice at least 10 working days before a show with FDA variance documentation; nothing above Class 2 less than 3 m above audience standing surfaces or within 2.5 m laterally.
audience_scanning: Audience locations limited to Class 1; scanning must not exceed Class 1 on the audience even in a scan failure

body: Department of Public Health Radiation Control Program
what: Class 3B and 4 facilities register and name a laser safety officer; 10 working days' notice for out-of-state lasers; entertainment lasers need an FDA variance and separations of 10 ft above and 8 ft to the side or below under continuous operator control.

body: Health and Safety Executive; local authorities
rule: General health and safety duties; HS(G)95 withdrawn
what: No laser show license. Duty holders must assess and control the risks and use competent contractors; HSE has withdrawn HS(G)95 and points to PLASA's guide.

rule: Guidance for the Safety of Display Lasers (2019)
what: Not compulsory; PLASA says following it will normally be enough to comply with the law and inspectors may cite it as good practice.

Notice of outdoor laser displays: CAP 736 says organizers should give 28 days' advance notification on form DAP 1918; the CAA's newer web page requests a minimum of 7 days. Legal backstop is Air Navigation Order 2016 articles 240, 241 and 265.

body: Employer, under federal occupational safety law
what: An employer who lacks the required expertise personally must appoint a laser safety officer (Laserschutzbeauftragter) with current training in writing before Class 3R, 3B or 4 lasers are operated.
Exposure limits must hold in the audience area up to 2.70 m; show area separated by a barrier at least 0.8 m high with 1 m lateral distance; a competent person verifies limits on site.
audience_scanning: Not banned outright: a beam in the audience space is treated as safe only if attenuated, widened, split or moved fast enough that limits are not exceeded

what: Written permission needed to aim a laser into navigable airspace; possessing a hand-held laser over 1 mW outside a private dwelling is prohibited within 10 km of airports and certified heliports and in the greater Montreal, Toronto and Vancouver regions.
Recommended ceilings at the closest audience point of 2.5 mW/cm2 for static beams and 10 mW/cm2 for continuously scanned beams; scan-fail shut-off target of 10 ms, preferably 1 ms.
audience_scanning: Supported within the MPE; ILDA members affirm that pulsed lasers should never be used
